subject: C02
required_fixes: [P1] RF01 — Coordinate reset with outstanding credential writes. In crates/desktop-core/src/authority.rs:1247, reset purges and removes the document without waiting for writes_in_flight. A previously admitted put can run after that purge. If its completion runs before settle_reset, its cleanup entry is subsequently erased by Data::default() at :1462; if it runs afterwards, the stale branch at :1306 adds an entry only in memory before attempting deletion. A crash or failed delete can therefore leave a credential permanently untracked after a reported successful reset. Preserve durable cleanup ownership across reset and prevent old writes from escaping the final purge. Acceptance: deterministic held-write tests exercise completion on both sides of reset settlement, failed cleanup and restart; every written record is deleted or durably recoverable, and reset never reports completion while an old write can recreate a credential.

[P1] RF02 — Retire context authority when reset is admitted. crates/desktop-core/src/authority.rs:1167 cancels existing operations but leaves active_ref and credential bindings valid until successful settlement. check_context ignores Resetting, read_scan_credential at :836 can still return a session credential, and the shared lifecycle admission at :788 can start new work after the initial cancellation. A failed reset never changes that reference. Invalidate the prior context at reset admission and block credential resolution/work admission throughout reset; recovery must issue fresh authority. Acceptance: hold reset pending and test old-context reads and operation admissions, then repeat with a failed reset; no prior reference becomes usable again.

[P1] RF03 — Distinguish uncommitted storage failure from a committed or uncertain replacement. crates/desktop-core/src/store.rs:215 renames the new document before a fallible directory open/fsync; authority.rs:536 treats every save error as proof of no change, restores the old in-memory Data and returns a refusal. Thus an import or endpoint change reported refused can appear after restart. During credential replacement, the disk can already contain retirement/cleanup entries even though memory and the refusal preserve the old capability. Reconcile post-rename failures or expose an explicit uncertain/committed state instead of blindly rolling back memory. Acceptance: inject failures before rename and after rename/during directory sync; receipt, snapshot, cleanup and restart state agree, with no refused operation silently applied later.

[P2] RF04 — Report and reconcile partial reset progress. In crates/desktop-core/src/authority.rs:1251, Keychain purge precedes the fallible store reset; purge itself can also delete some items before failing. settle_reset at :1471 retains every old Ready scan binding and can mark storage Ready whenever load succeeds. apps/desktop/src/features/tenants/tenants-settings.tsx then says 'Your data was kept' although credentials may already be deleted. Track partial progress, invalidate/reconcile affected credential capabilities and present accurate recovery information. Acceptance: test successful purge followed by store-reset failure, plus partial purge failure; snapshots and UI never claim deleted keys remain saved or all data was preserved, and restart/retry completes cleanup safely.
evidence_gaps: T06 interruption coverage is incomplete. crates/desktop-core/tests/context_credentials/main.rs:711 covers a purge that fails before changing anything and a normal reset; FileStore tests cover successful atomic replacement but no post-rename failure. The supplied 35 context/transport tests, 22 core tests and 12 native checks do not establish reset/write ordering, partial reset recovery or post-commit error semantics. Add production-interface fault tests for RF01–RF04 and bind fresh results to the repaired source.
optional_suggestions: Strengthen the new response validators in packages/desktop-contracts/src/client.ts. An independent in-memory execution of the production parser accepted an import review with discarded: {}, which renders missing counts; endpointReview.tenant and integer/count bounds are also unchecked. Validate the complete new DTO shapes and add malformed-response cases.

Retained logs report 33 frontend, 22 core, 35 context/transport, 12 IPC, 6 Keychain and 164 published-SDK unit tests passing. These are inspected implementer runs, not reviewer reruns.
